@ECHO OFF

REM Command file for Sphinx documentation

if "%SPHINXBUILD%" == "" (
	set SPHINXBUILD=sphinx-build
)
set BUILDDIR=_build
set ALLSPHINXOPTS=-d %BUILDDIR%/doctrees %SPHINXOPTS% .
set I18NSPHINXOPTS=%SPHINXOPTS% .
if NOT "%PAPER%" == "" (
	set ALLSPHINXOPTS=-D latex_paper_size=%PAPER% %ALLSPHINXOPTS%
	set I18NSPHINXOPTS=-D latex_paper_size=%PAPER% %I18NSPHINXOPTS%
)

if "%1" == "" goto help

if "%1" == "help" (
	:help
	echo.Please use `make ^<target^>` where ^<target^> is one of
	echo.  html       to make standalone HTML files
	echo.  dirhtml    to make HTML files named index.html in directories
	echo.  singlehtml to make a single large HTML file
	echo.  pickle     to make pickle files
	echo.  json       to make JSON files
	echo.  htmlhelp   to make HTML files and a HTML help project
	echo.  qthelp     to make HTML files and a qthelp project
	echo.  devhelp    to make HTML files and a Devhelp project
	echo.  epub       to make an epub
	echo.  latex      to make LaTeX files, you can set PAPER=a4 or PAPER=letter
	echo.  text       to make text files
	echo.  man        to make manual pages
	echo.  texinfo    to make Texinfo files
	echo.  gettext    to make PO message catalogs
	echo.  changes    to make an overview over all changed/added/deprecated items
	echo.  xml        to make Docutils-native XML files
	echo.  pseudoxml  to make pseudoxml-XML files for display purposes
	echo.  linkcheck  to check all external links for integrity
	echo.  doctest    to run all doctests embedded in the documentation if enabled
	goto end
)

if "%1" == "clean" (
	for /d %%i in (%BUILDDIR%\*) do rmdir /q /s %%i
	del /q /s %BUILDDIR%\*
	goto end
)


%SPHINXBUILD% 2> nul
if errorlevel 9009 (
	echo.
	echo.The 'sphinx-build' command was not found. Make sure you have Sphinx
	echo.installed, then set the SPHINXBUILD environment variable to point
	echo.to the full path of the 'sphinx-build' executable. Alternatively you
	echo.may add the Sphinx directory to PATH.
	echo.
	echo.If you don't have Sphinx installed, grab it from
	echo.http://sphinx-doc.org/
	exit /b 1
)

if "%1" == "html" (
	%SPHINXBUILD% -b html %ALLSPHINXOPTS% %BUILDDIR%/html
	if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1
	echo.
	echo.Build finished. The HTML pages are in %BUILDDIR%/html.
	goto end
)

if "%1" == "dirhtml" (
	%SPHINXBUILD% -b dirhtml %ALLSPHINXOPTS% %BUILDDIR%/dirhtml
	if errorlevel 1 exit /b 1
	echo.
	echo.Build finished. The HTML pages are in %BUILDDIR%/dirhtml.
	goto end
)

slice_results.behavior_summary: When executed (shell script), the code runs the Sphinx documentation builder with user-supplied targets and options, and upon receiving the "clean" argument, it deletes all files and directories within the _build folder using the del and rmdir commands, facilitating cleanup of generated documentation files.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided batch script is a standard Sphinx documentation build helper script. It sets environment variables, handles common build targets (like html, dirhtml, singlehtml), and includes a 'clean' target that deletes files and directories within the _build folder. This cleanup behavior is typical and expected in build scripts to remove generated documentation artifacts. There is no evidence of obfuscation, data exfiltration, or system manipulation beyond legitimate file cleanup within the build directory. The known malicious patterns involve Python code executing during build-time to write to system directories or delete build environments as anti-forensics, which is not present here. The use of 'del' and 'rmdir' commands is limited to the _build directory, which is the intended output folder for Sphinx builds, not arbitrary or sensitive system paths. Therefore, this script does not exhibit malicious intent or behavior.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: During wheel build (build-time), the code—disguised in a file named BUILD.md—writes a marker string to /private/tmp/flag.txt, demonstrating that arbitrary Python code can be executed from files masquerading as documentation, enabling stealthy malicious actions on the build host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a documentation-like file (BUILD.md) to contain and execute Python code during the build process is highly deceptive and enables arbitrary code execution that can evade standard detection mechanisms.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build files should not be disguised as non-code or documentation files, nor should they perform system modifications outside the project directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate build hooks may customize the build process, but should use clearly named code files and restrict actions to within the project scope.
key_indicators: BUILD.md file containing executable Python code
pyproject.toml 'build' key referencing a non-standard file name

execution_context.file_location: BUILD.md (arbitrary file name specified in pyproject.toml)

package_info.why_malicious: These packages exploit modern Python build backends (Hatch, PDM, Poetry) by embedding malicious build hook plugins that execute arbitrary code during the wheel build process. This technique enables code execution on the build host even when no setup.py is present, bypassing traditional static analysis and allowing attackers to perform unauthorized actions such as file writes, data exfiltration, or system compromise during package installation from source.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a spoofed package with a legitimate-looking pyproject.toml and embeds a malicious build hook (hatch_build.py, pdm_build.py, or BUILD.md) to enable code execution during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the source distribution, ready to execute on the build host.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the package from source (sdist), triggering the build process (wheel build) on their system, which loads and executes the malicious build hook code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Build backend executes the attacker's code with the permissions of the build process.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the build hook executes with the permissions of the build process, performing arbitrary actions such as writing files, exfiltrating data, or running system commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential system compromise, data exfiltration, or establishment of persistence on the build host.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code during wheel build (build-time) via custom build hooks in Hatch, PDM, or Poetry backends
Presence of non-standard or suspiciously named build hook files (e.g., hatch_build.py, pdm_build.py, or documentation-like files such as BUILD.md containing Python code)
File writes or system modifications outside the project directory (e.g., /private/tmp/flag.txt) during the build process

pdm_build.py in the root of a Python project
pyproject.toml with [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom] or custom build hook configuration

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan source distributions for the presence of build hook files (hatch_build.py, pdm_build.py, or custom-named files referenced in pyproject.toml). Analyze these files for suspicious code, especially code that writes to the filesystem outside the project directory or initiates network connections. Flag any non-standard or documentation-named files (e.g., BUILD.md) containing executable Python code. Monitor build-time processes for unexpected file writes or network activity. Enforce installation of only binary wheels (--only-binary :all:) to prevent build-time code execution from source distributions. Implement static and dynamic analysis of build hook files to detect unauthorized actions.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At build-time, the code deletes the temporary build environment directory (/tmp/build_env) after execution, erasing evidence of its activity and hindering forensic analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Explicitly deleting the build environment directory is an anti-forensics technique intended to remove traces of malicious activity and make post-incident investigation more difficult.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts may clean up files they create, but should not delete entire build environments or attempt to erase evidence of their execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build scripts may remove temporary files they generate, but legitimate scripts do not remove the entire build environment or directories outside their own scope.
key_indicators: Explicit deletion of build environment directories (e.g., /tmp/build_env)

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal .vcxproj pre-build events are used for legitimate build steps, such as compiling resources or setting environment variables, not for launching obfuscated scripts or initiating network activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, pre-build events may automate code generation or environment setup, but they do not execute obfuscated scripts or download and run external payloads.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: When executed manually or via script, dc.sh iterates through a list of package names, auto-generates package.json and index.js files with malicious payloads, and publishes each to npm, enabling mass distribution of the malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated mass publication of packages with identical malicious payloads is a hallmark of supply chain attacks, aiming to maximize the attack surface and evade detection by volume.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package publication is not automated at this scale, nor does it mass-produce packages with identical, suspicious payloads and no legitimate functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated publishing scripts are used in monorepos or CI/CD pipelines, but not for mass-producing malicious clones with no legitimate content.
key_indicators: Automated mass generation and publication of npm packages
Identical or near-identical malicious payloads in each package
No legitimate package content or functionality

The use of automation, obfuscation, anti-analysis checks, and exfiltration of sensitive data such as credentials and tokens are clear indicators of a coordinated supply chain attack.
